data.body:
=== HANDOFF #19 ADDENDUM — the stale-base CI trap RECURS. Rebase before every recheck. ===

The trap from #18 ADDENDUM 1 (CI takes the WORKFLOW from main but the CODE from the patchset) has now
bitten TWICE, with a DIFFERENT script each time:
  * change 1276 — `scripts/check_config_reads.py` missing (added by `3ad3abe72`)
  * change 1283 — `scripts/probe_rebar.py` missing, in the `golden-path (clean install)` job

**This is not a one-off; it is structural.** `main` is moving fast (other sessions are landing work
continuously), and every time a change adds a workflow step that invokes a NEW script, every in-review
change based before that commit starts failing CI with a missing-FILE error that looks nothing like a
stale base. On 1283 I wasted a full CI cycle treating it as a `golden-path` flake and re-running `recheck`
— it failed identically, which is what told me it was structural rather than transient.

**RULE: if a change has been in review for a while and CI fails on a missing file under `scripts/`,
REBASE FIRST — do not recheck.** A recheck re-runs the same stale tree and wastes a cycle (and, on a
stack, can cancel a sibling's run). `git ls-tree -r --name-only gerrit/main -- <path>` confirms the script
exists on main while your tree lacks it; that asymmetry IS the diagnosis.

Corollary worth internalising: **a change sitting in review decays.** The longer it waits for votes, the
more likely main has added a workflow-invoked script it cannot see. Prefer landing promptly over batching,
and rebase as a matter of course before re-requesting verification.

1283 has been rebased onto current `gerrit/main` (its ancestors 1279/1280 were already merged, so the
rebase correctly skipped them as applied cherry-picks) and re-pushed: 24 unit tests pass, live suite
collects 58.
